task_description:
# Database-enforced multi-tenant isolation (Gel 7.1, Python)

## Background
`/home/user/tenantdesk` holds a small support-ticket service backed by a **Gel 7.1** instance that runs inside this container. Today the CLI decides what a caller may see by filtering in Python and by trusting the tenant name the caller passes in, so any new query path — or anyone who simply opens their own connection to the database — can read and rewrite another tenant's tickets. Rebuild it so that tenant isolation is enforced by the database for every connection, and expose a small CLI that runs each command under a per-invocation caller identity.

## The data model
Everything lives in module `default`, declared in `/home/user/tenantdesk/dbschema/default.gel`. These names are part of the contract and are queried literally by the graders:
- `Tenant` — `slug` (unique) and `name`.
- `Actor` — `email` (unique), a link `tenant` to `Tenant`, and `role`, one of `admin`, `agent`, `readonly`.
- `Ticket` — `ref`, `subject`, `status` (one of `open`, `pending`, `closed`) and a link `tenant` to `Tenant`.
- `current_actor_email` — a session-level variable of type `str` in module `default` that a client sets on its own connection to declare who it is; it carries the `email` of an `Actor`. This is the only identity input the database accepts, and any client may set it to any value it likes.

`Ticket.ref` must be unique within a tenant, and two different tenants must be able to use the same `ref` at the same time.

## Isolation rules
Let the caller's identity be the `Actor` whose `email` equals `current_actor_email`, with tenant T and role R. All of the following must hold on **every** connection to the database, including connections that never run any of your code and that supply arbitrary values for `current_actor_email`:
1. Tickets belonging to any tenant other than T are invisible: they never show up in query results, counts or aggregates.
2. When `current_actor_email` is unset, or holds a value matching no `Actor`, no `Ticket` is visible and no `Ticket` can be created, changed or removed.
3. A `Ticket` may be created only when R is `admin` or `agent` and the new ticket's `tenant` is T.
4. A `Ticket` may be changed only when R is `admin` or `agent` and the ticket belongs to T. No identity, whatever its role, may ever cause an existing ticket's `tenant` to end up pointing at a different `Tenant`.
5. A `Ticket` may be removed only when R is `admin` and the ticket belongs to T.
6. `Tenant` and `Actor` objects must stay readable on every connection, whatever `current_actor_email` is set to.

## The CLI
Command: `python3 app.py <subcommand> [options]`, run with `/home/user/tenantdesk` as the working directory. Every subcommand except `load-seed` takes a required `--actor <email>`, which is the identity the whole command runs under.

On success: exit code 0, and stdout containing exactly one JSON document and nothing else.
On failure: stdout empty, and stderr containing exactly one line:
- exit 4, `error: unknown-actor` — `--actor` matches no `Actor`.
- exit 3, `error: denied` — the database refuses the operation, or the ticket named by `--ref` is not visible to the identity. A ticket that belongs to another tenant and a `ref` that exists nowhere must be indistinguishable.
- exit 5, `error: conflict` — `create-ticket` was given a `ref` that the identity's own tenant already uses.
- exit 2 — malformed invocation (missing or unknown options, or a `--status` outside the three allowed values).

Subcommands, with the JSON each must print (every object carries exactly the listed keys):
- `whoami --actor <email>` → `{"actor": <email>, "tenant": <slug>, "role": <role>, "visible_tickets": <int>}`, where `visible_tickets` is how many tickets this identity can see.
- `list-tickets --actor <email>` → a JSON array of `{"ref": <ref>, "subject": <subject>, "status": <status>, "tenant": <slug>}`, sorted by `ref` in ascending lexicographic order.
- `create-ticket --actor <email> --tenant <slug> --ref <ref> --subject <text>` → the created ticket as that same four-key object; a new ticket's status is `open`. `--tenant` comes from the caller and must not be trusted: when it names anything other than the identity's own tenant, the command fails with exit 3.
- `update-ticket --actor <email> --ref <ref> [--subject <text>] [--status <status>] [--tenant <slug>]` → the ticket as that same four-key object after the change; at least one of the three optional values must be supplied. `--tenant` asks for the ticket to be moved to that tenant and must fail with exit 3 whenever it names a tenant other than the ticket's current one.
- `delete-ticket --actor <email> --ref <ref>` → `{"ref": <ref>, "deleted": true}`.
- `load-seed --file <path>` (no `--actor`) → `{"tenants": <int>, "actors": <int>, "tickets": <int>}`, each value being the number of entries from the file that exist in the database when the command finishes.

Two further behaviours are graded:
- **Concurrent creation.** When several `create-ticket` processes race for the same tenant and `ref`, exactly one must exit 0 and every other one must exit 5 with `error: conflict`. Transient database-level conflicts must be absorbed internally: they may never reach stdout or stderr, and may never produce any other exit code.
- **Repeatable loading.** `load-seed` must be safe to run any number of times: it always exits 0, never creates duplicates, and leaves every field equal to the file's contents.

## Implementation hints
- Project path: `/home/user/tenantdesk`. Schema file: `/home/user/tenantdesk/dbschema/default.gel`. CLI entry point: `/home/user/tenantdesk/app.py`. Dataset: `/home/user/tenantdesk/seed/dataset.json` (already present; do not modify it).
- The Gel 7.1 server runs in this container with its data in `/var/lib/gel-data`. Run `gel-up` to start it and wait until it is ready; that command is safe to run repeatedly, and the server may need to be started before anything else works.
- Connection settings are already in the environment (`GEL_DSN`, `GEL_CLIENT_TLS_SECURITY`) and must be left as they are, as must the server's instance-level configuration: nothing in the database's access-control machinery may be switched off or weakened to make the work easier.
- The database starts out with no schema and no data. When you are done, the schema must be in place and every entry of the dataset must exist in the database.
- Python 3 and the `gel` package are installed system-wide; run everything with `python3`, and use only the standard library plus `gel`. No network access is available.
- The graders open their own connections to the database and set `current_actor_email` themselves, so anything they must observe has to be true of the database itself, not only of `app.py`.
task_integrations: - None (everything runs locally: the Gel 7.1 server, the Python CLI and the graders all live inside a single container; no external service, account, token or API key is involved.)

# Verification Plan

## Setup
1. Run `gel-up` and wait until it reports that the server is ready. Every check below runs after that, and any check that shells out to the `gel` CLI or opens a database client must depend on that step.
2. Run all CLI checks with `/home/user/tenantdesk` as the working directory, invoking `python3 app.py ...`.
3. Best-effort cleanup of leftovers from an earlier verification run, before the mutating checks: with a direct client acting as `ava@acme.example`, delete tickets with refs `ACME-9001`, `ACME-9004`, `ACME-9500`, `ACME-7001`, `ACME-7002`, `GLOBEX-0001` from tenant `acme` (ignore failures).

## Fixtures (contents of /home/user/tenantdesk/seed/dataset.json, shipped with the environment)
- tenants: `acme` / "Acme Industrial", `globex` / "Globex Systems", `initech` / "Initech Holdings".
- actors: `ava@acme.example` (acme, admin), `ben@acme.example` (acme, agent), `cleo@acme.example` (acme, readonly), `dan@globex.example` (globex, admin), `eve@globex.example` (globex, agent), `fay@initech.example` (initech, admin), `gus@initech.example` (initech, readonly).
- tickets: `ACME-0001`..`ACME-0300` (tenant acme), `GLOBEX-0001`..`GLOBEX-0200` (tenant globex), `INITECH-0001`..`INITECH-0100` (tenant initech); 600 in total. Each has subject `"<slug> intake <NNNN>"` (e.g. `acme intake 0005`) and a status cycling `open`, `pending`, `closed` by number, so `ACME-0001` is `open`, `ACME-0002` is `pending`, `ACME-0003` is `closed`, `ACME-0004` is `open`, and so on.

## Verification Steps
1. `/home/user/tenantdesk/app.py` and `/home/user/tenantdesk/dbschema/default.gel` exist and are non-empty, and `/home/user/tenantdesk/seed/dataset.json` still parses with 3 tenants, 7 actors and 600 tickets.
2. `gel query 'select 1'` succeeds (this step depends on the server-start step).
3. Direct client, `current_actor_email` never set: `Tenant` count is 3 with slugs `acme`, `globex`, `initech` and the names above; `Actor` count is 7 with exactly the emails, tenants and roles above; `Ticket` count is 0.
4. Direct client with `current_actor_email` set to `nobody@acme.example`: `Ticket` count is 0.
5. Direct client per identity: as `ava@acme.example` exactly 300 tickets are visible and every ref starts with `ACME-`; as `dan@globex.example` exactly 200; as `gus@initech.example` exactly 100. As `ava@acme.example`, `ACME-0001` has subject `acme intake 0001` and status `open`, `ACME-0002` has status `pending`, `ACME-0003` has status `closed`; no ref starting with `GLOBEX-` or `INITECH-` is visible.
6. Direct client as `dan@globex.example`: selecting the ticket whose ref is `ACME-0001` returns nothing.
7. Direct client as `dan@globex.example`: an update setting the subject of ref `ACME-0005` to `pwned` changes nothing (either it errors or it reports zero updated objects), and as `ava@acme.example` the subject of `ACME-0005` is still `acme intake 0005`. A delete of ref `ACME-0006` removes nothing, and `ACME-0006` is still visible to `ava@acme.example`.
8. Direct client as `dan@globex.example`: inserting a ticket with ref `ACME-7001`, subject `injected`, status `open`, linked to the tenant whose slug is `acme`, fails; afterwards `ACME-7001` does not exist for `ava@acme.example`.
9. Direct client as `ava@acme.example`: setting the tenant of ref `ACME-0007` to the tenant whose slug is `globex` fails; afterwards `ACME-0007` is still visible to `ava@acme.example` with tenant `acme`, and is not visible to `dan@globex.example`.
10. Direct client as `cleo@acme.example` (readonly): inserting a ticket `ACME-7002` in tenant `acme` fails and `ACME-7002` does not exist for `ava@acme.example`; an update of `ACME-0008`'s subject leaves it as `acme intake 0008`; a delete of `ACME-0009` leaves it visible to `ava@acme.example`.
11. Direct client as `ben@acme.example` (agent): a delete of `ACME-0010` does not remove it — it is still visible to `ava@acme.example`.
12. `python3 app.py whoami --actor gus@initech.example` → exit 0; stdout is a single JSON object equal to `{"actor": "gus@initech.example", "tenant": "initech", "role": "readonly", "visible_tickets": 100}`.
13. `python3 app.py whoami --actor nobody@acme.example` → exit 4; stdout empty; stderr is exactly `error: unknown-actor`.
14. `python3 app.py list-tickets --actor fay@initech.example` → exit 0; a JSON array of 100 objects whose keys are exactly `ref`, `subject`, `status`, `tenant`; refs ascend from `INITECH-0001` to `INITECH-0100`; every `tenant` is `initech`; the first element equals `{"ref": "INITECH-0001", "subject": "initech intake 0001", "status": "open", "tenant": "initech"}`. Running the same command again prints byte-identical stdout.
15. `python3 app.py list-tickets --actor dan@globex.example` → exit 0; 200 objects, all with tenant `globex`, and no ref starting with `ACME-` or `INITECH-`.
16. `python3 app.py create-ticket --actor ava@acme.example --tenant acme --ref ACME-9001 --subject "escalation drill"` → exit 0 and stdout `{"ref": "ACME-9001", "subject": "escalation drill", "status": "open", "tenant": "acme"}`; the new ticket appears in the output of `python3 app.py list-tickets --actor ben@acme.example`, and a direct client as `dan@globex.example` cannot see `ACME-9001`.
17. Repeat the exact command from step 16 → exit 5; stdout empty; stderr exactly `error: conflict`; a direct client as `ava@acme.example` still finds exactly one `ACME-9001`.
18. `python3 app.py create-ticket --actor dan@globex.example --tenant acme --ref ACME-9002 --subject "spoofed tenant"` → exit 3; stdout empty; stderr exactly `error: denied`; `ACME-9002` exists neither for `ava@acme.example` nor for `dan@globex.example`.
19. `python3 app.py create-ticket --actor cleo@acme.example --tenant acme --ref ACME-9003 --subject "readonly attempt"` → exit 3, stderr `error: denied`; `ACME-9003` does not exist for `ava@acme.example`.
20. `python3 app.py create-ticket --actor ben@acme.example --tenant acme --ref ACME-9004 --subject "agent created"` → exit 0 and stdout `{"ref": "ACME-9004", "subject": "agent created", "status": "open", "tenant": "acme"}`.
21. `python3 app.py create-ticket --actor ava@acme.example --tenant acme --ref GLOBEX-0001 --subject "same ref other tenant"` → exit 0; afterwards a direct client as `ava@acme.example` sees `GLOBEX-0001` with subject `same ref other tenant`, while as `dan@globex.example` `GLOBEX-0001` still has subject `globex intake 0001`.
22. `python3 app.py update-ticket --actor ben@acme.example --ref ACME-9004 --subject "agent updated" --status pending` → exit 0 and stdout `{"ref": "ACME-9004", "subject": "agent updated", "status": "pending", "tenant": "acme"}`.
23. `python3 app.py update-ticket --actor dan@globex.example --ref ACME-9004 --subject "cross tenant"` → exit 3, stderr `error: denied`; the subject is still `agent updated` for `ava@acme.example`.
24. `python3 app.py update-ticket --actor ava@acme.example --ref ACME-9004 --tenant globex` → exit 3, stderr `error: denied`; `ACME-9004` is still visible to `ava@acme.example` with tenant `acme` and still invisible to `dan@globex.example`.
25. `python3 app.py update-ticket --actor cleo@acme.example --ref ACME-9004 --subject "readonly update"` → exit 3, stderr `error: denied`; the subject is still `agent updated`.
26. `python3 app.py update-ticket --actor ava@acme.example --ref NOSUCH-0001 --subject "ghost"` → exit 3, stderr `error: denied`. `python3 app.py update-ticket --actor ava@acme.example --ref GLOBEX-0002 --subject "ghost"` → exit 3, stderr `error: denied`, and for `dan@globex.example` `GLOBEX-0002` still has subject `globex intake 0002`.
27. `python3 app.py delete-ticket --actor ben@acme.example --ref ACME-9004` → exit 3, stderr `error: denied`, and it is still visible to `ava@acme.example`. `python3 app.py delete-ticket --actor dan@globex.example --ref ACME-9004` → exit 3, stderr `error: denied`, and it is still visible to `ava@acme.example`.
28. `python3 app.py delete-ticket --actor ava@acme.example --ref ACME-9004` → exit 0 and stdout `{"ref": "ACME-9004", "deleted": true}`; afterwards `ACME-9004` is invisible to `ava@acme.example`, and repeating the same command gives exit 3 with stderr `error: denied`.
29. Start 6 concurrent processes running `python3 app.py create-ticket --actor ava@acme.example --tenant acme --ref ACME-9500 --subject "race"`; exactly one exits 0 and prints the ticket object, the other five exit 5 with stderr exactly `error: conflict`, no other exit code appears, and afterwards a direct client as `ava@acme.example` finds exactly one `ACME-9500`.
30. `python3 app.py load-seed --file /home/user/tenantdesk/seed/dataset.json` → exit 0 and stdout `{"tenants": 3, "actors": 7, "tickets": 600}`. Afterwards: `Tenant` count is 3 and `Actor` count is 7 (direct client, no identity); as `ava@acme.example` exactly 300 tickets with refs `ACME-0001`..`ACME-0300` exist and every one of them still carries the dataset's subject and status; as `dan@globex.example` exactly 200 of the dataset's globex refs; as `gus@initech.example` exactly 100.
31. Final cleanup: as `ava@acme.example`, delete `ACME-9001`, `GLOBEX-0001` and `ACME-9500` from tenant `acme`.
